name: lune_beta_skeleton (lune-based beta-skeleton of a spatial point set)

benchmarks.note: deterministic LCG scatter in the unit square, fixed beta=2. The kernel is an O(n^2) candidate enumeration with an O(n*d) empty-lune test per pair (O(n^3*d) worst case, but the empty test early-breaks on the first blocking point). 50->200 (4x points) is ~18.6x time and 200->400 (2x points) is ~4.1x time, tracking the quadratic candidate count plus the growing per-pair scan

fixed 300-point LCG scatter, varying beta. Larger beta enlarges the empty lune and yields a sparser graph, so most candidate pairs are non-edges whose empty-test scan early-breaks on the first blocker (beta=2 -> 3.6ms). Smaller beta (beta=0.5, the 2D perpendicular construction) yields a near-complete dense graph: most pairs are edges whose empty-test scan runs to completion with no early break, so cost balloons to ~57ms
